patients.summary: Healthy 27-year-old digital marketing specialist who joined in August 2024, started a prenatal vitamin before trying to conceive and became pregnant in May 2025. Tinea corporis of the left forearm twice in the pregnancy, treated by outside dermatology with topical clotrimazole. Listeria bacteremia at 36 weeks after deli meat and soft cheese, treated with 14 days of IV ampicillin, then a term vaginal delivery in February 2026.

Scanned to media, routed to PCP for review.

documents.title: New Patient Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
27F here to establish care. Moved her primary care here after her old office's physician retired; prior records reviewed (Pap 2022 NILM, immunizations complete as a child).

No concerns today. Works as a digital marketing specialist, mostly remote. Never smoked, does not drink. Two dogs at home. Exercises a few times a week.

PMH: none. PSH: tonsillectomy at age 6. Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
FH: mother with type 2 diabetes; father with hypertension.

ROS: negative in full.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well appearing. HEENT unremarkable, tonsils surgically absent. Thyroid not enlarged. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no organomegaly. Skin clear. No edema. Neuro grossly normal. Affect bright.
PHQ-2: 0.

A/P: healthy adult, preventive visit.
- Baseline CBC, CMP, lipids, TSH. A1c given her mother's diabetes. One-time HIV and hepatitis C screening, she agrees.
- Cervical screening: Pap 2022 normal, next due 2025.
- Flu and COVID vaccines when the fall supply arrives; nurse visit.
- Return yearly, sooner as needed. She has the practice number for calls and texts.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Wanda, all of Wednesday's blood work came back normal: blood counts, kidney and liver tests, cholesterol, thyroid and A1c (no sign of diabetes). HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. No changes needed. See you at your physical next summer.

documents.body: In for seasonal flu vaccine and 2024-2025 COVID vaccine. No fever today, no prior reactions, NKDA. Flu given L deltoid, COVID given R deltoid, lots and VIS dates in the immunization record. Waited 15 min in the lobby without issue.

documents.title: Telehealth Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit, patient at home, identity verified.

She is hoping to get pregnant this year and wanted to know what she should do beforehand. Cycles regular. No medications. Never smoker, no alcohol. Healthy, labs in August normal.

Discussed: start a prenatal vitamin with folic acid now, ideally at least a month before trying. Her immunization record shows MMR and varicella series complete. Pap due later this year, can be done by OB at the first prenatal visit or here. Let us know when she has a positive test and we will get her to an OB group.

Plan: prenatal vitamin 1 tab daily, sent to her pharmacy. No other changes.

documents.title: Positive test
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi! I took a home pregnancy test today and it's positive. First day of my last period was May 26. What do I do next? Still taking the prenatal vitamin every day.

documents.title: RE: Positive test
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Congratulations! Please come in tomorrow for a quick urine test to confirm, and we'll send the referral to an OB group. Keep taking the prenatal vitamin. If you have heavy bleeding or one-sided pain, call us right away.

documents.title: Nurse Visit: Pregnancy Test
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Urine hCG positive. LMP 5/26/25, about 4 1/2 weeks. G1. No bleeding or cramping. On prenatal vitamin daily. Referral to OB sent per PCP; she will call to set up the first prenatal visit at 8 weeks. Reviewed reasons to call.

documents.title: Rash on my arm
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Sorry to bug you again. I've had a really itchy rash on my left forearm for about 5 days, it's a circle and it's getting bigger. Photo attached. Is there anything I can put on it now that I'm pregnant?

documents.title: RE: Rash on my arm
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for the photo. Since you're newly pregnant I'd like a dermatologist to look at it and pick the treatment. They had an opening Monday the 30th at 2:30 and we've booked it for you. Until then avoid scratching and don't put any steroid cream on it.

medications.sig: Apply a thin layer to the rash and 2 cm of surrounding skin twice daily for 4 weeks

documents.title: Dermatology Consultation
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
Dermatology consultation. Visit date 06/30/2025. Received 07/02/2025.

Reason for referral: pruritic rash, left forearm, in early pregnancy.

History: 28-year-old woman, G1P0 at about 5 weeks by LMP, with one week of a very itchy rash on the left forearm. She reports it began as a small red ring that has slowly widened, clearing in the middle with a red scaly rim. A few weeks ago she began going to hot yoga classes at her gym and uses her own mat. She has two dogs that often sleep on her bed. No new soaps or lotions. No other rashes.
PMH: current pregnancy. PSH: tonsillectomy in childhood.
Medications: prenatal vitamin daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: maternal type 2 diabetes, paternal hypertension.
Social: digital marketing; never smoker; no alcohol.

Exam: Left forearm with two annular, erythematous plaques, each with a raised scaly border and central clearing. Remainder of the exposed skin, scalp and nails unremarkable.

KOH preparation from the leading edge: branching septate hyphae.

Assessment: tinea corporis, left forearm.

Plan:
1. Clotrimazole 1% cream twice daily to the plaques and a margin of normal skin, 4 weeks. A topical azole is appropriate in pregnancy; no oral antifungal.
2. Wash towels and bedding in hot water; keep the area dry.
3. Return if not clearing in 4 weeks or if it spreads.

Thank you for this referral.
Dermatology

OB new prenatal visit, 07/21/2025. Copy to primary care.

G1P0 at 8w0d by LMP 05/26/2025. Transvaginal dating ultrasound today: single intrauterine pregnancy, crown-rump length consistent with 8w0d, cardiac activity present. EDD 03/02/2026 by LMP, confirmed by ultrasound.

Feels well; mild nausea, no vomiting. No bleeding. On prenatal vitamin. Recently treated by dermatology for tinea on the left forearm with clotrimazole cream, improving.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: BP and weight per our flowsheet, normal. Pelvic exam normal. Pap collected.

Prenatal labs drawn today: CBC, HIV, hepatitis B surface antigen, RPR, urine culture; results normal (attached). Pap NILM.

Plan: routine prenatal care, visits every 4 weeks, anatomy ultrasound at 18-20 weeks, glucose challenge at 24-28 weeks.
Obstetrics

OBSTETRIC ULTRASOUND, ANATOMY SURVEY. Exam date 10/06/2025. Received 10/09/2025.
Indication: routine anatomy survey, 19w0d by dates.
Findings: single live intrauterine pregnancy, cephalic. Fetal heart rate normal. Biometry consistent with dates; estimated fetal weight appropriate for gestational age. Fetal anatomy surveyed and normal, including brain, face, spine, four-chamber heart and outflow tracts, abdominal wall, kidneys, bladder and limbs. Placenta posterior, clear of the cervix. Amniotic fluid normal. Cervical length normal.
Impression: normal anatomy survey; growth appropriate for dates.

documents.title: Dermatology Follow-up
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
Dermatology follow-up. Visit date 10/13/2025. Received 10/16/2025.

Seen here 06/30 for tinea corporis of the left forearm, which cleared with 4 weeks of clotrimazole. She is now 20 weeks pregnant. For the past week the same area has been itching intensely again: ring-shaped patches with a red, flaky edge that are spreading outward and paler in the middle. She has kept going to hot yoga since early summer on her own mat, and the two dogs still sleep on the bed.
Medications: prenatal vitamin.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: two annular erythematous plaques on the left forearm with raised scaly borders and central clearing. No other sites involved.

KOH preparation: branching septate hyphae.

Assessment: recurrent tinea corporis, left forearm, likely reinfection from a household or gym source.

Plan:
1. Restart clotrimazole 1% cream twice daily and continue for 2 full weeks after the skin looks clear.
2. Wipe down the mat after every class and wash it weekly; shower soon after class.
3. Have the dogs checked by their veterinarian for ringworm; keep them off the bed until then.
4. Return if it recurs again.
Dermatology

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD. Regional hospital ED, seen 02/04/2026. Received by the practice 02/09/2026.

CC: fever and aches, 36 weeks pregnant.

HPI: 28F G1P0 at 36w2d (EDD 03/02/2026) with two days of fever, feeling run down and diffuse muscle aches. Also some mild crampy lower abdominal discomfort and a little more vaginal discharge than usual. Denies fluid leaking or contractions. No travel, no one sick at home. Pregnancy uncomplicated to date per patient and OB records. On questioning, she ate deli meats from the fridge and imported soft cheeses at a family picnic five days ago. History of tinea corporis of the forearm this pregnancy, treated by dermatology, resolved.
Meds: prenatal vitamin. Allergies: NKDA.
PSH: tonsillectomy. Social: never smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: T 38.6 C (101.5 F); other vitals per nursing flowsheet. Fatigued appearing, alert and oriented. Neck supple, no meningismus. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen gravid, soft, uterus nontender. No CVA tenderness. Fetal heart tones present, reassuring on monitoring.

Labs: WBC 14.6, mild leukocytosis. BMP and lactate within normal limits. UA negative. Urine and blood cultures (2 sets) sent.

MDM: febrile illness in late pregnancy after high-risk foods; concern for listeriosis. Started ampicillin 2 g IV every 4 hours after cultures. Discussed with OB on call; admitted to the obstetric service for IV antibiotics and fetal monitoring.
Disposition: admitted, stable.

documents.title: Discharge Summary, Obstetric Service
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY. Admitted 02/04/2026 from the ED, discharged 02/08/2026. Received 02/09/2026.

Diagnosis: listeriosis (Listeria monocytogenes bacteremia) in pregnancy, 36 weeks.

Course: 28-year-old G1P0 admitted at 36w2d with fever after eating deli meat and soft cheese. Started on ampicillin 2 g IV every 4 hours in the ED after cultures. Both admission blood culture sets grew Listeria monocytogenes, ampicillin-susceptible, reported 02/06. She was afebrile from hospital day 2 and the myalgias and cramping settled. Repeat blood cultures 02/06 negative (final no growth). Continuous and then twice-daily fetal monitoring reassuring; nonstress tests reactive throughout. No contractions, membranes intact, no labor.

A PICC line was placed in the right arm on 02/07 for home infusion.

Discharge medications: ampicillin 2 g IV every 4 hours via home infusion, last dose 02/17/2026 to complete 14 days; prenatal vitamin daily.
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: home infusion nursing for PICC care and removal; OB clinic twice weekly for nonstress tests until delivery; primary care this week. Return for fever, contractions, leaking fluid or decreased fetal movement. Avoid deli meats, unpasteurized cheeses and refrigerated smoked fish for the rest of the pregnancy.
Obstetrics

documents.title: In the hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Wanted you to know I'm in the hospital since yesterday with a fever. They think it might be listeria from something I ate. Baby is ok on the monitor. They've got me on IV antibiotics.

documents.title: RE: In the hospital
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you for telling me, Wanda. You're in the right place, and starting antibiotics early matters most. I'll watch for the hospital records. Message me when you're home and we'll set up a video visit.

documents.title: Telehealth Visit: Post-Discharge
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit, patient at home, identity verified.

Admitted 2/4-2/8 at 36 weeks with Listeria bacteremia; ED record and discharge summary reviewed. On ampicillin 2 g IV q4h by home infusion through 2/17, PICC right arm. Infusion nurse visiting; pump working.

Feels much better. No fever since the hospital. Aches gone. No contractions or leaking, baby moving well. PICC site looks clean on camera, no redness or swelling in the arm. Seeing OB twice a week for NSTs.

A/P: listeriosis in pregnancy, responding to treatment.
- Finish the full 14 days; infusion nurse to pull the PICC after the last dose.
- Call for fever, arm swelling or redness at the line, or any OB warning signs.
- Reviewed foods to avoid for the rest of the pregnancy, per the discharge instructions.
- Will see her in clinic after the baby comes.

documents.title: Home Infusion Nursing Visit
documents.author: home infusion RN
documents.body:
Home infusion nursing visit 02/18/2026. Received 02/19/2026.
IV ampicillin course completed with the final dose 02/17/2026, 14 days total. No missed doses. Afebrile. Right arm PICC removed intact today, tip intact, pressure held, site clean and dry with dressing applied. No arm swelling. Patient instructed on site care. Discharged from home infusion services.

documents.title: Delivery Discharge Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OBSTETRIC DISCHARGE SUMMARY. Admitted 02/23/2026 in labor, discharged 02/25/2026. Received 02/27/2026.

29-year-old G1P0 at 39w0d, admitted in spontaneous labor. Antepartum course notable for Listeria bacteremia at 36 weeks treated with 14 days of IV ampicillin (completed 02/17), blood cultures cleared. Afebrile throughout labor.

Uncomplicated spontaneous vaginal delivery 02/23/2026 of a liveborn girl, 3240 g, Apgars 8 and 9. Placenta delivered intact. Pediatrics examined the newborn given the maternal infection: well appearing, no signs of infection, routine newborn care.

Postpartum course routine; mother afebrile and well. Now G1P1.
Discharge medications: prenatal vitamin daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: OB postpartum visit in 6 weeks; pediatrics for the baby.
Obstetrics

documents.title: She's here
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Just wanted to share our daughter arrived on the 23rd! Everything went smoothly and the pediatrician said she's perfect. I'm tired but feeling good. Should I keep taking the prenatal vitamin?

documents.title: RE: She's here
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Congratulations to you all! So glad it went smoothly after February. Yes, keep taking the prenatal vitamin for now. Let's see you in clinic after your OB postpartum visit; the front desk will reach out to schedule.

documents.title: Obstetrics: Postpartum Visit
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Postpartum visit 04/06/2026, 6 weeks after an uncomplicated vaginal delivery. Copy to primary care.
Feeling well. Bleeding stopped. No fevers. Sleeping when the baby sleeps; good support at home. Postpartum mood screen normal.
Exam: BP normal. Breasts normal. Abdomen soft, uterus involuted. Perineum healed. 
Assessment: normal postpartum recovery. Continue prenatal vitamin. Routine gynecologic care; next Pap per screening guidelines. Return to primary care for general care.
Obstetrics

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
29F, about 11 weeks after a vaginal delivery on 2/23, here to check in. Baby with her, doing well.

Interval: Listeria bacteremia at 36 weeks, 14 days IV ampicillin, PICC out 2/18, cultures cleared. Delivered at term, uncomplicated; newborn well per pediatrics. OB postpartum visit 4/6 normal.

Today: feels good, tired in the expected way. No fevers since February. No rash on the arm since November. Mood good; PHQ-9 3. Eating and sleeping okay for a new parent. Still on the prenatal vitamin.

Exam: vitals as charted, weight down to 66 kg. Well appearing. Old PICC site right arm healed. Heart regular, lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Left forearm skin clear. No edema.

A/P:
1. Listeriosis, resolved. No further testing needed.
2. Postpartum, well. CBC today to check her counts after the infection and delivery.
3. Tinea corporis, no recurrence.
4. Health maintenance: Pap 07/2025 NILM. Flu and COVID vaccines this fall. Rebook the physical she postponed last year for late summer.

documents.title: Your blood count
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Wanda, your blood count from yesterday is normal: no anemia, white count back in the normal range. Nothing to do. Enjoy the summer with her.
